subject: general
question: Who was the first chairman of Finance Commission of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**KC Neogy**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kshitish Chandra Neogy:-**

 
 
• He was an Indian politician and economist.
 
• He was a member of the Indian Constituent Assembly and served as the first Finance Minister of India from 1951 to 1952.
 
• He was also a member of the Interim Government of India from 1946 to 1947 and served as the Minister of Relief and Rehabilitation.
 
• **He was appointed Chairman of the First Finance Commission of India.**
 
• The commission was tasked with determining the distribution of revenue between the central government and the states.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ashok Kumar Chanda:-**

 
 
• He was an Indian economist who played a key role in shaping India's economic policies in the post-independence era.
 
• He served as a member of the Planning Commission from 1950 to 1967 and was instrumental in formulating the Second and Third Five-Year Plans, which laid the foundation for India's economic development.
 
• Chanda was also a strong advocate for decentralization and self-reliance, and his ideas helped to shape India's mixed economy model..
 
 
 
• **K. Santhanam:-**
 
 
• He was an Indian politician, lawyer, and writer.
 
• He was a member of the Indian Constituent Assembly and served as the Union Minister for Railways and Transport from 1948 to 1952.
 
• He was also the Chairman of the Santhanam Committee, which investigated corruption in the Indian government. 
 
 
 
• **Pakala Venkataramana Rao Rajamannar:-**
 
 
• He was an eminent Indian jurist and politician who served as the Chief Justice of the Madras High Court from 1948 to 1961.
 
• He was also the first Indian to hold this esteemed position.
 
• Additionally, he held the position of acting Governor of Madras State from 1957 to 1958.
 
• Rajamannar was a distinguished figure in the legal fraternity, widely respected for his intellectual prowess, impartiality, and dedication to upholding justice.
